summary_en: Archive documents cover the Ferry Building as a Port of San Francisco property, including a 1983 final environmental impact report on the Ferry Building complex (the Embarcadero, World Trade Center, Agriculture Building and Pier One), a 1971 northern-waterfront comprehensive plan, and Port Commission minutes on repairs to correct damage sustained by the building, on plaza planting, and on grant funds for the Ferry Building renovation and restoration project. The building is operated by the Port of San Francisco, whose FY2025 budget line is $156M; no place-specific city contract appears in this data.

The Ferry Building and environs should be revived as a major gateway to the city. The BART platform should include a terminal area for commuter ferry boats, and this terminal area should be able to accommodate additional ferry service as may be developed in the fu- ture. A heliport, if located in the immediate vicinity of the Ferry Build- ing, should be located south of the Ferry Building and should have direct access to the ferries and land-based transit systems in the Ferry Building area in order to facilitate distribution of commuters and visi- tors to downtown and waterfront areas. 13. should be extended to the central public plaza at Fisherman's Wharf and extended farther into Victorian Park in order to assist visitors and residents alike in free movement by public transit to the Northern Waterfront. In addition, a minirail system should be explored to link Victorian Park to the Ferry Building. This minirail system could also be used to complement the existing cable car lines in order to provide a complete loop for use by tourists and to make available additional parking south of Market Street during the peak parking demand periods at Fisher- man*s Wharf. Consideration should be given to extending the minirail system to Yerba Buena Center. 16. The elevated portion of the Embarcadero Freeway from south of the Ferry Building to Broadway should be replaced by a sub-surface freeway system. This action would greatly enhance the many develop- ments in the immediate vicinity and would once again establish the Ferry Building as a focal point and termination for Market Street.
